sasha: Heads up — bringing up pegasus-rt13b int4 on staging and seeing a clear quality regression on our summarization eval (ROUGE-L -4.2, hallucination rate +6%). perplexity on validation set is basically unchanged which makes me suspect token->embed alignment rather than model weights.
ben: Ugh. Any reproducible prompt + config? which quant pipeline did you use (gptq/awq/ours)?
sasha: Ran our standard int4 pipeline (rwi-quant v0.9, per-channel PQ + adaptive clipping). Config: 
```
model: pegasus-rt13b
quant: int4
scheme: per-channel
clip: adaptive
tokenizer-normalize: auto
```
li: Can you paste the eval diff and a short log snippet? also did you try running float16 host to confirm baseline?
sasha: Float16 baseline looks fine. Eval summary (short):
- baseline fp16 rouge-l: 42.8
- int4 rouge-l: 38.6
- hallucination metric (entity halluc count / doc): baseline 0.12 => int4 0.18

Log snippet when decoding a failing example: 
```
WARN tokenizer: mapped unknown bytes -> <unk> for 0xE2 0x82
E KVCACHE: token_map mismatch at idx 1023: expected 789 actual 790
```
maria: That token_map mismatch screams vocabulary offset (special token or normalization change). Did the tokenizer conversion script change recently? We had a tokenizer normalizer patch last week (nfkc fallback) in the repo.
ben: I ran a quick bisect locally: the regression appears when using the new tokenizer normalizer commit (repo@a1b2c3) — it changed NFC/NFKC behavior for some punctuation sequences; that will shift multi-byte sequences -> different token ids for some inputs. If kvcache was precomputed or if embedding table indexing assumptions differ, that could explain it.
sasha: Hmm — we did convert the model artifacts using the upstream converter after the normalizer change. converter command used: 
```
python -m rwi.convert --model peg-rt13b --vocab /artifacts/peg-vocab.json --out /deploy/peg-rt13b-conv.bin --token-offset 0
```
li: Two possible root causes: (1) vocab mapping order changed so embedding indices no longer align with converted params, causing consistent but subtle semantic shift; (2) rotary/positional parameter head mapping changed (headwise vs shared) and quantization math exposing it.

maria: I reproduced locally by toggling tokenizer normalizer: nfkc vs nfd. With nfkc we match fp16 behaviour; with nfd we get the int4 regression. So it's the normalizer for sure.
ben: Nice. Quick mitigation options: 
- revert tokenizer normalizer on the deploy path and re-run conversion (simple, short-term)
- add a token_id_offset remap step in converter to re-align embedding indices (safer if vocab reorder is intentional)
- create a canary variant with forced nfkc normalization and run weighted rollout
sasha: For immediate customer-facing safety I'm leaning to canary + token_id_offset fallback. I patched the converter to accept `--token-id-offset` and ran a smoke: 
```
python -m rwi.convert --model peg-rt13b --vocab /artifacts/peg-vocab.json --out /deploy/canary.bin --token-id-offset -1
```
That recovered a lot of the quality on the problematic dataset (rouge-l recovers ~+3). Not perfect but buys time.

triage-bot: automated-eval: canary.bin vs fp16 baseline: rouge-l delta -1.1, hallucination delta +0.9%. Tags: needs-human-review

li: Follow-ups: 
1) Add a unit regression test in our eval harness that runs a short prompt set through tokenizer+converter+inference to catch token remap changes (sample 12 seeds).
2) Update tokenizer conversion docs to pin normalization mode explicitly.
3) Run a full conversion + int4 quant sweep on the nfkc-normalized vocab; compare against current artifacts.

maria: I'll own the unit test and docs. ben — can you write a small script that calculates a stable hash of the vocab->index mapping so the converter can refuse to run if a mapping unexpectedly changed? That would have caught this earlier.

ben: Yep, I'll open a PR with a sanity check that prints a mapping diff and fails with non-empty diff unless `--force-remap` is set. Also adding a tiny perf test to ensure token_id_offset is zero by default.

sasha: Great. Deployment plan: 
- roll canary with token-id-offset patch (5% traffic) + realtime eval dashboard
- if stable over 24h, roll 25% and regenerate full quant conversions under pinned normalizer
- long-term: ensure tokenizer normalizer changes require an explicit conversion artifact regen and a check-in to the model onboarding checklist

li: One more note — we should audit other models that recently ran conversion with `tokenizer-normalize: auto` because this change could affect several families (llama/mistral/gemma/qwen). I'll run a quick grep and post results.

maria: thanks. I'll attach the failing example and short reproduction notebook to the PR.

sasha: attaching sample failing prompt here: "Summarize the following long email thread about contract terms — pay attention to parties and effective dates." With nfkc mismatch the output invents a party name sometimes because token splitting moved punctuation into different tokens which then mixed into generation.

ben: Noted. Okay next steps tracked in PR #1429. :thumbsup:
